correctness.rationale: With the finite pointed initial model s_I, ten-atom vocabulary and goal Phi_G fixed, Achilleos Section 3 constructs for each binary-PCP instance B only a varying finite action library Act_B consisting of add_i events plus three fixed verification actions. Theorem 3.19 gives B has a match iff a finite plan reaches Phi_G. The full construction has no postconditions and event preconditions of modal depth at most one. Since finite action words and finite product updates can be enumerated and effectively checked, membership in Sigma^0_1 holds. Binary PCP is many-one complete via effective injective prefix coding, proving equality. Fixed does not mean the number/size of actions is bounded. Checked the source theorem and quantifier localization, not just the abstract.
residual_risks: Depends on the precise finite designated-point semantics and source event construction; no independent reimplementation of PCP event models.

originality.rationale: Achilleos 2026 already gives a fully specified many-one PCP reduction with exactly the fixed initial state, fixed goal, fixed vocabulary and only actions varying. The new theorem is a direct corollary of the original reduction plus the elementary enumeration upper bound, even though the source paper advertises only undecidability in its abstract. value.rationale: The question which input parameter carries undecidability is intrinsically significant, but in this exact formulation the answer is already visibly encoded in Achilleos Section 3. The only added step is the standard r.e. upper bound obtained by enumerating finite plans. No independent new boundary, restriction, certificate or mathematically motivated unknown invariant survives. Thus it is a textbook corollary/explicit restatement, not a new valuable mathematical contribution.
residual_risks: A differently restricted planning variant could be valuable, but none is proved in the frozen claim.
